gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch creates a comprehensive PermCodes.java interface with nested interfaces for all 7 domains (Channel, Merchant, Payment, IAM, System, Develop, Device) containing ~40 menu code constants, 11 action constants, and 4 name constants. It also creates a migration script (migrate-perm-codes.mjs) and updates 92 controller files to replace string literals with PermCodes constant references. The patch is massive (~6000 lines) and addresses all stated requirements.
base_vs_gold_expectation: Base correctly fails: the test patch adds 'import cn.daxpay.open.platform.core.code.PermCodes' and uses 'PermCodes.Action.VIEW' in an annotation, but PermCodes.java does not exist in the base commit, causing a compilation error. Gold correctly passes: PermCodes.java is created with Action.VIEW = "view", making the test compile and the assertion assertEquals("payment:merchant:view", ...) succeed since the resolved value is unchanged.
too_narrow_risks: Test only verifies PermCodes.Action.VIEW exists and equals "view" — a candidate creating just 'interface PermCodes { interface Action { String VIEW = "view"; } }' would pass
None of the ~40 menu code constants are tested (e.g., Channel.Merchant.MENU, System.Protocol.MENU, Payment.Order.MENU)
None of the other 10 action constants are tested (MANAGE, PUBLISH, UPDATE, STATUS, SIGN, KICKOUT, RESET_PASSWORD, ASSIGN_ROLE, RESEND, TEST)
No name constants tested (Channel.Merchant.VIEW_NAME_CN, VIEW_NAME_EN, MANAGE_NAME_CN, MANAGE_NAME_EN)
Zero controller migration is verified — the issue explicitly requires updating controllers across platform and channel modules (92 files in gold patch), but the test checks none
No verification of the nested interface domain structure (7 domains required)
Only tests one full code resolution path; doesn't verify constants are usable as annotation attributes beyond the single example
implementation_coupling: The test expects the exact path 'PermCodes.Action.VIEW' which is dictated by the issue specification, so this coupling to the API naming is appropriate and not a gold-implementation artifact
environment_risks: Maven build with '-am' flag compiles all upstream modules in a large multi-module Java project — transient build failures or missing cached dependencies could cause false negatives
The build requires Java 21 (-Djava.version=21); Docker image must have this configured correctly
mismatches: task.toml labels category as 'debugging' but the issue is clearly a refactoring/feature-addition task (creating centralized constants and migrating usages)

evidence.detail: Test patch only changes one annotation from string literal to PermCodes.Action.VIEW and adds the PermCodes import — verifies only one constant out of ~55 defined in the gold patch

Existing test has 2 test methods: resolveFullCode_shouldJoinMenuCodeAndActionCode and resolveFullCode_withoutMenuCode_shouldReturnActionCodeOnly. Both test PermCodeUtil.resolveFullCode, not the existence of PermCodes constants.
Test runner: mvn -Djava.version=21 -pl daxpay-platform/daxpay-platform-core -am -Dtest=PermCodeUtilTest test — only runs tests in daxpay-platform-core, none of the 92 controller modules
Gold patch modifies 94 files (1 migration script, 1 new PermCodes.java, 92 controllers) but the test only validates a trivial subset
category = 'debugging' is incorrect for this refactoring/feature task

summary: The test is severely too narrow for this large refactoring task. The gold patch creates a 321-line PermCodes interface with ~55 constants across 7 domain namespaces and migrates 92 controller files, but the test only verifies that PermCodes.Action.VIEW exists and equals "view". A trivial 3-line PermCodes class with just that one constant would pass. The test should be expanded to verify: (1) representative constants from each domain (menu codes, action codes, name constants), (2) at least a sample of controller migrations, and (3) the compile-time constant property for annotation attributes. The category metadata is also wrong (labeled 'debugging' instead of 'refactoring').
